description: Only Laboratory records with WBC strictly above 6.5 pass the filter; records with exactly 6.5 are excluded.

b.request: Filter Laboratory rows to WBC > 6.5 (exact 6.5 excluded), group by CENTROMEA with NULL as its own group, compute each group's average of non-null (GOT − GPT) and (APTT − PT) over rows where both operands are present, then return one unrounded row with the unweighted mean of the per-group AST − ALT averages and the unweighted mean of the per-group APTT − PT averages, ignoring groups whose per-group value is NULL.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(ast_alt) AS avg_ast_minus_alt, AVG(aptt_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM (SELECT CENTROMEA, AVG(GOT - GPT) AS ast_alt, AVG(APTT - PT) AS aptt_pt FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 GROUP BY CENTROMEA) AS group_avgs;
b.raw: Filter Laboratory rows to WBC > 6.5 (exact 6.5 excluded), group by CENTROMEA with NULL as its own group, compute each group's average of non-null (GOT − GPT) and (APTT − PT) over rows where both operands are present, then return one unrounded row with the unweighted mean of the per-group AST − ALT averages and the unweighted mean of the per-group APTT − PT averages, ignoring groups whose per-group value is NULL.

c.request: Taking individual lab records and using 6.5 as the white blood cell count (`WBC`) cutoff, group them by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`), treating a missing status as its own group, and for each status work out the average AST minus ALT (`GOT` − `GPT`) and the average APTT minus PT (`APTT` − `PT`), skipping records where a difference can't be computed. Then give me a single row with two unrounded figures: the average of those per-status AST − ALT averages and the average of the per-status APTT − PT averages, with each status counting equally and missing per-status values ignored. Only Laboratory records with WBC strictly above 6.5 pass the filter; records with exactly 6.5 are excluded.
c.sql: WITH per_status AS (SELECT CENTROMEA, AVG(GOT - GPT) AS ast_alt_avg, AVG(APTT - PT) AS aptt_pt_avg FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 GROUP BY CENTROMEA) SELECT AVG(ast_alt_avg) AS avg_ast_minus_alt, AVG(aptt_pt_avg) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt FROM per_status;

a.request: Looking at individual lab records with a white blood cell count (`WBC`) strictly greater than 6.5, group them by anti-centromere status (`CENTROMEA`), treating a missing status as its own group, and for each status work out the average AST minus ALT (`GOT` − `GPT`) and the average APTT minus PT (`APTT` − `PT`), skipping records where a difference can't be computed. Then give me a single row with two unrounded figures: the average of those per-status AST − ALT averages and the average of the per-status APTT − PT averages, with each status counting equally and missing per-status values ignored.
a.sql:
WITH per_status AS (
  SELECT CENTROMEA,
         AVG(GOT - GPT) AS avg_ast_minus_alt,
         AVG(APTT - PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE WBC > 6.5
  GROUP BY CENTROMEA
)
SELECT AVG(avg_ast_minus_alt) AS avg_ast_minus_alt,
       AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
FROM per_status;

d.request: Keep Laboratory records with WBC strictly greater than 6.5 (exclude WBC = 6.5), group them by CENTROMEA with NULL as its own group, average GOT−GPT and APTT−PT per group (skipping rows where either input is NULL), then return the unrounded mean of the group AST−ALT averages and the unrounded mean of the group APTT−PT averages, one row.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(ast_alt_avg) AS avg_ast_alt_mean, AVG(aptt_pt_avg) AS avg_aptt_pt_mean FROM (SELECT CENTROMEA, AVG(GOT - GPT) AS ast_alt_avg, AVG(APTT - PT) AS aptt_pt_avg FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 GROUP BY CENTROMEA) AS grouped;
